act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023 / Indian Penal Code (IPC) 1860
title: Theft
keywords: theft stolen property stealing robbery shoplifting
plain_text: Theft is the dishonest taking of movable property out of the possession of any person without consent. Punishment: imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both. Aggravated theft (house-breaking, vehicle theft) carries higher punishment.

act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023 / Indian Penal Code (IPC) 1860
title: Extortion
keywords: extortion blackmail threat money coercion demand threat harm
plain_text: Whoever intentionally puts a person in fear of injury and dishonestly induces them to deliver property or valuable security commits extortion. Punishment: imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both.

act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023 / Indian Penal Code (IPC) 1860
title: Voluntarily causing hurt
keywords: assault beating hit punch slap hurt injury physical attack fight
plain_text: Voluntarily causing hurt (causing bodily pain, disease or infirmity) to another person is punishable with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to Rs. 1000 or both. Grievous hurt carries up to 7 years imprisonment.

act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023 / Indian Penal Code (IPC) 1860
title: Assault or criminal force on woman / Sexual harassment
keywords: sexual harassment molestation outrage modesty woman assault touch inappropriate
plain_text: Assault or criminal force on a woman intending to outrage her modesty is punishable with imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and fine. Sexual harassment of woman at workplace is separately covered under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act 2013 (POSH Act).

act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023 / Indian Penal Code (IPC) 1860
title: Rape
keywords: rape sexual assault sexual violence non consensual sex
plain_text: Rape is punishable with rigorous imprisonment of minimum 10 years extendable to life imprisonment and fine. The survivor can report to any police station. A female officer must record the statement. Medical examination must be done with survivor's consent.

act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023 / Indian Penal Code (IPC) 1860
title: Cheating
keywords: cheating fraud deceive false promise online fraud money scam fake
plain_text: Cheating by deceiving a person and dishonestly inducing them to deliver property or to do something they would not otherwise do. Punishment: imprisonment up to 7 years and fine. Online fraud additionally covered under IT Act Section 66C and 66D.

act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023 / Indian Penal Code (IPC) 1860
title: Criminal intimidation / Threat
keywords: threat intimidation threatening harm death injury reputation
plain_text: Threatening someone with injury to their person, reputation or property to cause alarm or to make them do something they are not legally bound to do. Punishment: imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both. Threat of death or grievous hurt: up to 7 years.

act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023 / Indian Penal Code (IPC) 1860
title: Defamation
keywords: defamation reputation false statement slander libel social media post fake news
plain_text: Making or publishing any imputation about a person intending to harm their reputation is defamation. Punishment: imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both. Truth and public good are valid defences. Online defamation also attracts IT Act provisions.

act: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023 / Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) 1973
title: First Information Report (FIR)
keywords: FIR police complaint first information report register complaint cognizable offence
plain_text: An FIR is the first step in reporting a cognizable offence (serious crimes like theft, assault, rape, murder). Police CANNOT refuse to register an FIR for a cognizable offence. If police refuse, you can: (1) Send complaint by post to SP/DSP, (2) Approach Magistrate under Section 156(3), (3) File complaint directly in court. A copy of the FIR must be given to the complainant FREE of charge.

act: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023 / Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) 1973
title: Zero FIR
keywords: zero FIR police station jurisdiction wrong station any police station
plain_text: A Zero FIR can be filed at ANY police station regardless of where the offence occurred. The station that receives it must forward it to the police station having jurisdiction. Very useful when you are not in the right area or don't know which station has jurisdiction.

act: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023 / Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) 1973
title: Arrest without warrant
keywords: arrest police arrest rights arrest warrant illegally detained custody arrested
plain_text: Police can arrest without a warrant only for cognizable offences. Rights upon arrest: (1) Right to know the grounds of arrest, (2) Right to inform a friend or relative, (3) Right to consult and be defended by a lawyer, (4) Right to be produced before Magistrate within 24 hours, (5) Right to bail in bailable offences. Illegal detention or third-degree methods can be challenged by Habeas Corpus petition in High Court.

act: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023 / Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) 1973
title: Anticipatory Bail
keywords: anticipatory bail arrest fear bail before arrest pre arrest bail
plain_text: If a person has reason to believe they may be arrested for a non-bailable offence, they can apply to the Sessions Court or High Court for anticipatory bail. If granted, the police must release them on bail if arrested. Application must show reasons why arrest is feared.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005
title: Domestic Violence — Protection, Residence and Monetary Orders
keywords: domestic violence husband wife family abuse physical emotional verbal financial dowry beating
plain_text: Any woman who has been in a domestic relationship and is subjected to domestic violence (physical, sexual, verbal, emotional, economic abuse) can approach a Magistrate for: (1) Protection Order — prohibiting abuser from committing acts of violence, (2) Residence Order — right to stay in shared household, (3) Monetary Relief — maintenance and compensation, (4) Custody Order for children. A Protection Officer or lawyer can help file an application. FIR can also be filed under IPC Section 498A (cruelty by husband/relatives).

act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023 / Indian Penal Code (IPC) 1860
title: Cruelty by husband or relatives (Dowry harassment)
keywords: dowry harassment dowry demand cruelty husband in-laws torture 498A
plain_text: Cruelty by husband or relatives — including dowry demands, mental or physical harassment — is a criminal offence punishable with imprisonment up to 3 years and fine. Cognizable and non-bailable. File FIR at local police station. Also covered under Dowry Prohibition Act 1961.

act: Consumer Protection Act 2019
title: Consumer Rights and Consumer Forum
keywords: consumer complaint defective product bad service online shopping refund cheated purchased goods services
plain_text: A consumer who has paid for goods or services and suffered deficiency or unfair trade practice can file a complaint. Forums: District Commission (claims up to Rs. 1 crore), State Commission (Rs. 1-10 crore), National Commission (above Rs. 10 crore). Complaint can be filed online at consumerhelpline.gov.in. No lawyer needed for District Commission. Relief: refund, replacement, compensation, damages. Limitation: 2 years from cause of action.

act: Consumer Protection Act 2019
title: Definition of Consumer and Deficiency
keywords: consumer definition service deficiency defective product warranty guarantee online shopping ecommerce
plain_text: Consumer: Any person who buys goods or hires services for personal use (not for resale). Includes online purchases. Deficiency: Any fault in quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard. Defective goods: Any fault making it unsafe or not meeting standards. E-commerce sellers are also covered.

act: Transfer of Property Act 1882 / Rent Control Acts (State-specific)
title: Landlord-Tenant — Eviction and Notice
keywords: landlord tenant eviction notice rent house locked out illegal eviction security deposit
plain_text: A landlord CANNOT evict a tenant without proper legal notice and court order. For month-to-month tenancy: 15 days notice required. Annual tenancy: 6 months notice. Forceful eviction, locking the premises, or cutting utilities without court order is ILLEGAL and constitutes criminal trespass and wrongful restraint. The tenant can: (1) File FIR for illegal eviction, (2) Approach Rent Controller, (3) File civil suit. State Rent Control Acts provide additional protection. Security deposit must be returned.

act: Indian Contract Act 1872
title: Valid Contract and Breach of Contract
keywords: contract agreement breach promise broken deal signed agreement not paid refund service not provided
plain_text: A valid contract requires: offer, acceptance, consideration (payment/value), free consent, lawful object, and competent parties. Breach: If one party fails to perform, the other can claim compensation for actual losses (Section 73). Unlawful contracts (illegal, immoral, against public policy) are void. Limitation period to file civil suit for contract breach: 3 years.

act: Information Technology Act 2000 (IT Act) and Amendment 2008
title: Cybercrime — Hacking, Identity Theft, Online Fraud
keywords: hacking cyber crime phishing identity theft OTP fraud online fraud fake account social media hack password stolen
plain_text: Key IT Act offences: Section 66 (hacking/computer damage), Section 66C (identity theft — using another's password/OTP), Section 66D (cheating by impersonation online), Section 67 (publishing obscene material). Report cybercrimes at cybercrime.gov.in or nearest Cybercrime police station. For financial fraud: also report to bank immediately and RBI Ombudsman.

act: Information Technology Act 2000 — IT (Intermediary Guidelines) Rules 2021
title: Non-consensual intimate image sharing (Revenge Porn)
keywords: private photos videos leaked revenge porn morphed images intimate images shared without consent
plain_text: Sharing private intimate images without consent is an offence under IT Act Section 66E (violation of privacy — up to 3 years and fine) and Section 67/67A (obscene/sexually explicit material online). File complaint at cybercrime.gov.in and local police. Social media platforms must remove such content within 24 hours of reporting.

act: Right to Information Act 2005 (RTI)
title: RTI — Getting Government Information
keywords: RTI right to information government document transparency application public authority record
plain_text: Any citizen can request information from any public authority (government department, PSU, etc.). How to file RTI: Write application to Public Information Officer (PIO) of the relevant department, pay Rs. 10 fee (exempted for BPL), submit in person or by post or online at rtionline.gov.in. Response time: 30 days (48 hours if life/liberty at stake). If PIO refuses, appeal to First Appellate Authority then Central/State Information Commission. PIO can be penalized for non-response.

act: Motor Vehicles Act 1988 and Amendment 2019
title: Road Accident — Hit and Run, Compensation
keywords: road accident car accident hit and run vehicle accident injury death compensation insurance claim
plain_text: In road accident: (1) Immediate duty to help injured and report to nearest police station. (2) Hit and run victims can claim compensation from Solatium Fund (Ministry of Road Transport). (3) Accident compensation claim: File before Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT). No-fault liability (Section 140): Rs. 50,000 for death, Rs. 25,000 for grievous hurt — no need to prove negligence. Fault liability (Section 166): Higher compensation based on income and negligence. Insurance company is mandatory party.

act: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012 (POCSO)
title: Child Sexual Abuse — POCSO
keywords: child abuse sexual abuse minor child molestation POCSO child pornography
plain_text: POCSO protects children (under 18) from sexual assault, sexual harassment, and pornography. All offences are cognizable and non-bailable. Reporting is MANDATORY for anyone who has knowledge of offence (failure to report is itself an offence). Child-friendly procedures: statement recorded at home or comfortable place, no repeated questioning, in-camera trial. Report to police or CHILDLINE 1098.

act: Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989
title: Atrocities against SC/ST — Rights and Procedures
keywords: caste discrimination SC ST atrocity untouchability caste abuse humiliation land grab
plain_text: Intentional insult, intimidation, land grabbing, forced labour, social boycott against SC/ST members is a cognizable, non-bailable offence. Special courts (SC/ST Courts) handle these cases. Victim entitled to compensation, relief, rehabilitation. A senior police officer (DSP level) must personally investigate. Bail is not easily granted to the accused.

act: Industrial Disputes Act 1947 / Payment of Wages Act 1936 / Shops and Establishments Acts
section: ID Act Section 25F, 25G; Wages Act Section 3, 4
title: Labour Rights — Unfair Dismissal, Unpaid Wages
keywords: fired job terminated dismissed wrongful termination salary not paid dues not cleared unpaid wages labor
plain_text: Employer cannot retrench a permanent worker (in establishments with 100+ workers) without: 3 months notice or pay in lieu, retrenchment compensation (15 days wages per year of service), government permission. Unpaid wages: Complaint to Labour Commissioner or Payment of Wages Authority within 1 year. Remedy: reinstatement, back wages, or compensation. Wrongful dismissal: approach Labour Court.

act: Negotiable Instruments Act 1881
title: Cheque Bounce
keywords: cheque bounce dishonoured cheque returned cheque insufficient funds bounced cheque loan
plain_text: Cheque bouncing for insufficient funds or other technical reasons: Payee must send written notice within 30 days of cheque return. Drawer has 15 days to pay. If unpaid, file criminal complaint in court within 30 days after 15-day notice period. Punishment: imprisonment up to 2 years or twice the cheque amount or both. This is a compoundable offence (can be settled by payment). Also file civil suit for recovery separately.

act: Specific Relief Act 1963 / Code of Civil Procedure (CPC) 1908
section: Specific Relief Act Section 10, 38; CPC Order 39
title: Civil Injunction — Stopping Someone from Doing Something
keywords: injunction stop court order restrain someone civil court property dispute construction encroachment
plain_text: When immediate action is needed to prevent irreversible harm (e.g., someone demolishing your property, encroachment), you can apply for a temporary injunction in civil court. The court can pass an ex-parte (one-sided, emergency) injunction the same day in urgent cases. Limitation for civil suits varies by type of dispute (generally 3 years for contract, 12 years for property).

act: Constitution of India
title: Fundamental Rights — Personal Liberty and Writ Petitions
keywords: fundamental rights personal liberty illegal detention habeas corpus writ petition high court supreme court government violation
plain_text: Article 21: Right to life and personal liberty. Article 22: Protection against arbitrary arrest (right to know grounds, right to lawyer, produced before magistrate in 24 hours). Article 32: Right to approach Supreme Court for enforcement of fundamental rights (Writ Petition). Article 226: Right to approach High Court. Habeas Corpus: If someone is illegally detained, High Court can order their release. Police brutality, custodial violence, or illegal detention can be challenged.

act: Limitation Act 1963
title: Limitation Periods — Deadlines to File Cases
keywords: limitation period deadline time limit file case expired missed deadline court case how long
plain_text: Key limitation periods in India: Contract disputes — 3 years from breach. Property disputes — 12 years (possession), 3 years (money). Tort/personal injury — 3 years. Consumer forum — 2 years from cause of action. Cheque bounce — 1 month to file after notice period. FIR — No limitation for serious crimes. Limitation can be extended if fraud, mistake, or disability caused delay. Missing a deadline can permanently bar a claim — act promptly.

act: Legal Services Authorities Act 1987
title: Free Legal Aid
keywords: free legal aid lawyer poor no money legal help DLSA SLSA legal services authority
plain_text: Free legal aid is a constitutional right (Article 39A). Eligible persons: those with annual income below specified limit, SC/ST, women, children, disabled, industrial workers, victims of disaster, persons in custody. Apply to: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) at every district court, State Legal Services Authority (SLSA), or NALSA (National). They provide free lawyers, legal advice, mediation. Lok Adalats can settle disputes amicably.

act: Indian Evidence Act 1872 / Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023
title: Evidence — What is admissible, Electronic evidence
keywords: evidence proof electronic evidence screenshot WhatsApp message email video CCTV admissible court
plain_text: Electronic evidence (screenshots, WhatsApp messages, emails, call recordings, CCTV footage) is admissible in Indian courts under Section 65B of Evidence Act (certificate required for electronic records). Confession to police is NOT admissible. Confession made freely before Magistrate is admissible. Preserve original devices and do not delete or alter digital evidence. Take screenshots with timestamps visible. Get a Section 65B certificate if possible.

act: Dowry Prohibition Act 1961
title: Dowry — Giving, Taking or Demanding
keywords: dowry demand marriage jewelry gold money in-laws husband family demand gifts
plain_text: Giving or taking dowry is illegal. Demanding dowry is punishable with imprisonment minimum 6 months, maximum 2 years, and fine Rs. 10,000 or value of dowry (whichever is more). Stridhan (wife's own gifts and property) must be returned to her on demand. Dowry death (Section 304B IPC/BNS Section 80) — if woman dies within 7 years of marriage due to burns/injury connected to dowry demand, presumption of dowry death arises against husband and in-laws.

act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act 2013 — POSH Act
title: Workplace Sexual Harassment (POSH)
keywords: sexual harassment workplace office boss colleague POSH ICC internal complaint committee unwanted advances
plain_text: Every employer with 10+ employees must have an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC). Complaint must be filed within 3 months of incident. ICC inquiry must be completed within 90 days. Relief: warning, termination of harasser, compensation. If no ICC or employer doesn't act: file complaint with Local Complaints Committee (LCC) at District level. Police complaint under IPC/BNS is also an option. Government employees can approach Sexual Harassment Complaints Committee.

act: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act 2007
title: Senior Citizen Rights — Maintenance and Property
keywords: old parents elderly abandoned maintenance children support senior citizen property transfer
plain_text: Children (including adopted) and grandchildren are legally obligated to maintain parents and grandparents. If neglected, senior citizens can apply to Maintenance Tribunal (Sub-Divisional Officer level). Can get up to Rs. 10,000/month maintenance. If property was transferred to children and they neglect parents, the transfer can be declared VOID. Abandoning senior citizens in care homes, hospitals etc. is a criminal offence.
